stem: A transplant candidate asks why the evaluation includes many organ-specific tests rather than one standard panel for every patient. Which explanation aligns with standard evaluation education?

options.text: Transplant programs define organ-specific protocols to validate end-organ disease and overall health for safe transplantation
Every candidate receives identical testing regardless of organ or comorbidities
Diagnostic testing is optional once psychosocial evaluation is complete
Only blood type testing is required before listing

explanation.rationale_correct: Evaluation education explains that transplant programs define organ-specific diagnostic protocols to confirm end-organ disease and determine whether the patient can safely undergo transplantation.

rationale_incorrect.B: References describe individualized, organ-specific evaluation protocols rather than one identical test panel for all candidates.
rationale_incorrect.C: Diagnostic testing is a required component of evaluation, not replaced by psychosocial assessment alone.
rationale_incorrect.D: Listing requires comprehensive evaluation beyond blood type alone.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → evaluation process → c. Diagnostic testing → i.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Transplant programs define organ-specific protocols for diagnostic studies

stem: During post-transplant infection-prevention teaching, a recipient asks what personal practice is emphasized as a best method to reduce infection risk at home. Which teaching point is correct?

options.text: Frequent hand-washing, including before meals and after contact with secretions
Avoiding all contact with the transplant team after discharge
Stopping immunosuppression when at home to reduce infection risk
Relying only on antibacterial gel and never using soap and water

explanation.rationale_correct: Infection-prevention education instructs recipients to wash hands frequently as a best practice, including before preparing or eating meals and after contact with excretions or secretions.

rationale_incorrect.B: Recipients maintain transplant team contact; infection prevention does not replace team communication.
rationale_incorrect.C: Immunosuppression must continue as prescribed; stopping therapy increases rejection and infection risk.
rationale_incorrect.D: Hand hygiene includes soap and water when hands are visibly soiled; gel supplements but does not replace washing when needed.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → i. Hand hygiene
primary_anchor.quote_hint: hand-washing is a best practice to prevent

stem: Which health-maintenance tests may be required during transplant evaluation to remain current with national prevention guidelines?

options.text: Mammogram, Papanicolaou test, bone densitometry, and colonoscopy as age- and gender-appropriate
Elective cosmetic surgery assessment for all candidates
Routine dental extraction for every candidate regardless of dentition
Annual lung allocation score recertification for kidney candidates

explanation.rationale_correct: Evaluation references include age- and gender-specific health maintenance testing such as mammography, Papanicolaou testing, bone densitometry, and colonoscopy per national prevention guidelines.

rationale_incorrect.B: Cosmetic surgery assessment is not listed among required health-maintenance screening tests.
rationale_incorrect.C: Dentition is assessed, but routine extraction for every candidate is not a universal evaluation requirement.
rationale_incorrect.D: LAS applies to lung allocation, not kidney candidate health-maintenance screening.

stem: During living kidney donor education, which disclosure must transplant programs provide regarding program performance?

options.text: Program-specific recipient patient and graft survival rates compared with national SRTR data
A guarantee that every donated kidney will function perfectly for 20 years
The donor's personal MELD score after donation
Confidential refusal codes from unrelated deceased-donor offers

explanation.rationale_correct: Living donor education requires disclosure of program-specific patient and graft survival rates and how those rates compare with national SRTR data.

rationale_incorrect.B: Donor education discusses risks and outcomes; perfect long-term graft function cannot be guaranteed.
rationale_incorrect.C: MELD scoring applies to liver waitlist candidates, not living kidney donors.
rationale_incorrect.D: Unrelated deceased-donor refusal codes are not part of living donor outcome disclosure.
